topic: Ambedkar & the Making of the Constitution

items.title: Ambedkar: Life, Education & Ideas
items.body:
## Early life & education

- **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** was born on **14 April 1891 at Mhow** (Madhya Pradesh) in a **Mahar** family that faced severe untouchability.
- Studied at **Elphinstone College, Bombay**, then took an **MA and PhD in economics from Columbia University** (New York), a **D.Sc. from the London School of Economics**, and qualified as a **barrister from Gray's Inn**, London.
- One of the most highly educated leaders of his generation, he fused **economics, law and social theory** in his campaign against caste.

## Core ideas

- Caste is not merely a division of labour but a **division of labourers** enforced by graded inequality; its cure is the **annihilation of caste**, not reform of it.
- Championed **constitutional methods, education and political power** for the Depressed Classes — 'Educate, Agitate, Organise'.
- His economics thesis *The Problem of the Rupee* influenced the design of the **Reserve Bank of India**.
keyPoints: Born 14 April 1891 at Mhow in a Mahar family.
PhD (Columbia), D.Sc. (LSE), Barrister (Gray's Inn) — one of the most educated leaders of his era.
Slogan: 'Educate, Agitate, Organise'; sought caste annihilation, not reform.
His thesis The Problem of the Rupee informed the design of the Reserve Bank of India.
items.mnemonic: 'CLG' education trail = Columbia → LSE → Gray's Inn.

items.title: Ambedkar's Social Movements & Organisations
items.body:
## Landmark satyagrahas

- **Mahad Satyagraha (1927):** asserted the right of Depressed Classes to draw water from the public **Chavdar tank** at Mahad; at a follow-up conference the **Manusmriti was publicly burned** (25 Dec 1927).
- **Kalaram Temple Entry (Nashik, 1930):** demanded temple entry for the Depressed Classes.

## Organisations & journals

| Vehicle | Year | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Mooknayak | 1920 | First journal (aided by Shahu of Kolhapur) |
| Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha | 1924 | Welfare & education of Depressed Classes |
| Bahishkrit Bharat | 1927 | Marathi fortnightly |
| Independent Labour Party | 1936 | Contested 1937 provincial polls |
| Scheduled Castes Federation | 1942 | Political platform |
| Republican Party of India | 1956/57 | Founded (realised after his death) |

## Constitutional advocacy

- Represented the Depressed Classes at **all three Round Table Conferences (1930–32)** and won **separate electorates** in the **Communal Award (1932)**.
- Gandhi's fast-unto-death led to the **Poona Pact (Sept 1932)**: separate electorates were replaced by **reserved seats within a joint electorate** (raised from 71 to 148 in the provinces).
keyPoints: Mahad Satyagraha (1927): Chavdar tank water rights + burning of the Manusmriti.
Kalaram Temple Entry movement launched at Nashik in 1930.
Mooknayak (1920) and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) were his early mobilising tools.
Communal Award (1932) gave separate electorates; the Poona Pact replaced them with reserved seats.
Political parties: Independent Labour Party (1936) → Scheduled Castes Federation (1942) → RPI (1956/57).

items.title: Constituent Assembly: Demand, Formation & Composition
items.body:
## From idea to Assembly

- **1934:** the idea of a Constituent Assembly is first advanced by **M.N. Roy**.
- **1935:** the **INC** formally demands one; **1938:** Nehru insists it be composed of elected Indians.
- **1940:** conceded in principle (**August Offer**); **1942:** the **Cripps Mission** promises it after WWII.
- **1946:** finally set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan**; elections held **July 1946**; first meeting **9 December 1946**.

## Composition

| Category | Seats |
|---|---|
| British provinces | 292 |
| Chief commissioners' provinces | 4 |
| Princely states | 93 |
| **Total** | **389** |
| After partition | **299** |

- Members were **indirectly elected** by provincial assemblies via **proportional representation / single transferable vote** (1 seat ≈ 10 lakh people); princely-state seats were filled by their rulers' nominees.
keyPoints: Idea first proposed by M.N. Roy (1934); INC demanded it in 1935.
Constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946; elections July 1946; first meeting 9 Dec 1946.
Planned strength 389 seats (292 + 4 + 93 princely states); reduced to 299 after partition.
Members indirectly elected by proportional representation with a single transferable vote.

items.title: Office-bearers & the Objectives Resolution
items.body:
## Presiding officers

| Role | Person | Date |
|---|---|---|
| First (provisional) President | Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha | 9 Dec 1946 |
| Permanent President | Dr. Rajendra Prasad | 11 Dec 1946 |
| Vice-President | H.C. Mukherjee | — |
| Constitutional Advisor | Sir B.N. Rau | — |

- Sinha presided as the **oldest member** before Rajendra Prasad's election.

## Objectives Resolution

- Moved by **Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946** and **adopted on 22 January 1947**.
- Declared India an **independent sovereign republic**, guaranteeing justice, equality and liberty and safeguards for minorities and depressed classes.
- Its ideals were carried almost verbatim into the **Preamble** of the Constitution.
keyPoints: Provisional President Sachchidananda Sinha; permanent President Rajendra Prasad (11 Dec 1946).
H.C. Mukherjee was Vice-President; B.N. Rau the Constitutional Advisor.
Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru on 13 Dec 1946, passed on 22 Jan 1947.
The Objectives Resolution became the philosophical basis of the Preamble.

items.title: Committees & the Drafting Committee
items.body:
## Major committees & chairmen

| Committee | Chairman |
|---|---|
| Union Powers / Union Constitution | Jawaharlal Nehru |
| States (negotiating) / Provincial / Advisory | Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel |
| Drafting Committee | Dr. B.R. Ambedkar |
| Rules of Procedure Committee | Dr. Rajendra Prasad |

- The Assembly worked through **8 major and several minor committees** and held **11 sessions**.

## Drafting Committee

- Constituted on **29 August 1947** with **seven members**:
  1. **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman)**
  2. K.M. Munshi
  3. **Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar** (Telugu jurist, Madras Presidency)
  4. N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar
  5. Syed Mohammad Saadulla
  6. N. Madhava Rau (replaced B.L. Mitter)
  7. T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan)
- It shaped the working draft into the final Constitution, earning Ambedkar the title **'Father of the Indian Constitution'**.
keyPoints: Union committees chaired by Nehru; States/Advisory by Patel; Drafting by Ambedkar; Rules by Rajendra Prasad.
Drafting Committee set up 29 August 1947 with seven members.
Members included K.M. Munshi, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Saadulla, Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari.
Ambedkar's stewardship earned him the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

items.title: Timeline, Andhra Members & Legacy
items.body:
## Making of the Constitution — key dates

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 9 Dec 1946 | First meeting (Sinha presiding) |
| 13 Dec 1946 | Objectives Resolution moved |
| 22 Jan 1947 | Objectives Resolution adopted |
| 29 Aug 1947 | Drafting Committee formed |
| 26 Nov 1949 | Constitution **adopted/enacted** |
| 26 Jan 1950 | Constitution **came into force** |

- Total time taken: about **2 years, 11 months and 18 days**.

## Andhra members of the Assembly

- **Durgabai Deshmukh** (founder, Andhra Mahila Sabha), **Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar** (Drafting Committee), **N.G. Ranga**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Tanguturi Prakasam** ('Andhra Kesari'), **Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy**, **Moturi Satyanarayana**.

## Ambedkar's later career & legacy

- Independent India's **first Law Minister**; **resigned in 1951** partly over the stalling of the **Hindu Code Bill**.
- **Embraced Buddhism at Nagpur (14 Oct 1956)** with lakhs of followers; died **6 Dec 1956**.
- Founder of the **Republican Party of India**; awarded the **Bharat Ratna (1990)** posthumously.
keyPoints: Adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950; took about 2 years 11 months 18 days.
Andhra members: Durgabai Deshmukh, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, N.G. Ranga, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, T. Prakasam.
Ambedkar was first Law Minister; resigned 1951 over the Hindu Code Bill.
Converted to Buddhism at Nagpur on 14 Oct 1956; died 6 Dec 1956; Bharat Ratna 1990.

items.title: Other Members, Symbols & Framing Facts (PYQ set)
items.body:
## Notable Constituent Assembly members (beyond the office-bearers)

- **K.C. Neogy** — a member of the Constituent Assembly who later chaired the **First Finance Commission (1951)**.
- Other members frequently paired in exams: **H.C. Mukherjee** (Vice-President), **G.V. Mavalankar** (Speaker of the legislative wing), **Frank Anthony** (Anglo-Indians), **H.P. Modi** (Parsis), **Begum Aizaz Rasul**.

## National symbols adopted by the Assembly

| Symbol | Adopted on |
|---|---|
| **National Flag** | **22 July 1947** |
| **National Anthem** ('Jana Gana Mana') & **National Song** ('Vande Mataram') | **24 January 1950** |
| **State Emblem** (Lion Capital of Sarnath) | 26 January 1950 |

## Framing facts & figures

- The Assembly held **11 sessions** over **2 years, 11 months and 18 days**; the Constitution was signed by members on **24 January 1950**.
- Total expenditure ≈ **₹64 lakh**.
- **Prem Behari Narain Raizada** hand-wrote (calligraphed) the original Constitution; **Nandalal Bose** and team illustrated it.
- The Assembly also served as the **provisional Parliament** (1950–52) until the first general elections.
keyPoints: K.C. Neogy was a Constituent Assembly member and chaired the First Finance Commission (1951).
National Flag adopted 22 July 1947; National Anthem & Song adopted 24 January 1950.
The Constitution was signed on 24 Jan 1950; framing took 2 years 11 months 18 days over 11 sessions.
Total cost of framing ≈ ₹64 lakh; original hand-calligraphed by Prem Behari Narain Raizada, illustrated by Nandalal Bose.
The Constituent Assembly acted as the provisional Parliament until the 1951–52 elections.
items.mnemonic: Flag 22 Jul 1947; Anthem/Song 24 Jan 1950 — flag before freedom, songs before Republic Day.
